Q: How should an interview portfolio distinguish implemented behavior, measured evidence and remaining assumptions?
A:
Present a concrete user problem, system boundaries, a runnable path and observed failure/recovery behavior. Link claims to reproducible commands, source versions and results under stated conditions.

Distinguish a local fixture from an authenticated integration, a single-worker test from distributed recovery and an automated accessibility scan from human approval. Explain a decision you changed after evidence contradicted it. A strong portfolio helps an interviewer inspect reasoning and limits, rather than requiring belief in a broad 'production ready' label.
Why: A local Kafka replay test can demonstrate one commit-before-ack failure boundary. It does not establish multi-broker availability or rebalance correctness unless those conditions were also executed and recorded.
Risk: Overstated claims make genuine implementation evidence harder to trust.
Trade: A scoped, reproducible result is more defensible than an unsupported coverage checklist.
Try: Prepare a five-minute demo with normal behavior, one injected failure and an honest evidence ledger.
